title: Sebastian and the Salt
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars go out, Hazel Voss—the last oath-bound swordspeaker—discovers his small charms were the only thing keeping the dying dragon-fire beneath the city alive. The country's magic was never outlawed; it was hoarded by the Salt Court, who sealed the borders to feed it. With a runaway ward-keeper named Sebastian and a disgraced salt-tithe collector, Hazel must cross a nation that officially no longer exists to reach the First Hearth before the last dragon-fire gutters out. In the end, Hazel breaks his own oath to speak the fire free, dissolving the Salt Court's claim and leaving the inheritance of magic—not to kings, but to everyone who stayed.
about_author: Emrys Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated grimoires in a coastal customs house. They write fantasy about people who keep promises no one asked them to make.

chapters.title: Charms for a Starless Night
chapters.summary: Hazel Voss sells a luck-knot to a fisherman's daughter as the stars vanish overhead. POV: Hazel. When the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass, his dormant oath-sword flares awake for the first time in three years. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—the quiet life he built is already over, and he knows it before anyone tells him.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Kept the Door
chapters.summary: Hazel finds Sebastian, a twelve-year-old ward-keeper's apprentice, alone at the collapsed gatehouse, refusing to leave his post because 'someone has to hold the door.' POV: Hazel. A salt-wraith attack forces them to flee together. The beat is reluctant responsibility hardening into protectiveness; Hazel recognizes in Sebastian the child he once was, sworn to a duty that abandoned him.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Official decrees declare the realm dissolved; roads are lawless, tolls meaningless. POV: Sebastian. The pair falls in with Maren Quill, a salt-tithe collector whose job—and identity—evaporated overnight. Sebastian, starved for family, begins orbiting both adults. The beat is bittersweet humor: three strangers pretending they haven't already decided to stay together.

chapters.title: What the Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren reveals the tithe she collected wasn't tax—it was fuel, funneled to the hidden Salt Court to feed captive dragon-fire. POV: Maren. Her guilt surfaces as precision: maps of every collection route, every hearth that went cold. Hazel realizes his outlawed charms worked only because they skimmed leaked fire. The beat is complicity; all three have been feeding the machine that starved them.

chapters.title: The Guttering Road
chapters.summary: Traveling the old tithe-route toward the First Hearth, they pass villages where magic-starved wards fail one by one. POV: Hazel. Hazel spends charm after charm saving strangers, thinning his own reserves. Sebastian secretly gives away his last ward-stone to a sick girl. The beat is sacrifice as inheritance—what you give away is what you actually own.

chapters.title: Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: The Salt Court's knights intercept them, offering Hazel restoration of his oath and rank if he surrenders Sebastian, whose blood can re-key the wards permanently. POV: Sebastian. He overhears the offer and runs, forcing a chase through burning salt-flats. The beat is betrayal anticipated and survived; Sebastian learns found family means choosing people who choose you back.

chapters.title: The Oath-Bound Lie
chapters.summary: Cornered, Hazel finally reads the full text of his inherited oath—and discovers it binds him to the Salt Court, not the people. His whole rebellion has been treason by design. POV: Hazel. Maren talks him back from despair: oaths are words; justice is what you do inside them or against them. The beat is the theme crystallized—law and justice are not the same thing.

chapters.title: First Hearth
chapters.summary: They breach the Salt Court's vault and find the last dragon-fire caged in a hearth the size of a cathedral, tended by chained fire-priests. POV: Maren. The Court's Lord Tithe offers Hazel everything—pardon, power, Sebastian's safety—if he speaks the binding renewed. The beat is temptation at its most reasonable; the villain's offer would save everyone except the future.

chapters.title: The Breaking Word
chapters.summary: Climax. Hazel speaks the counter-oath, shattering his own sword and the binding together; the dragon-fire floods free through every broken ward in the land. Sebastian holds the collapsing door open—his post, finally honored—as Maren turns the tithe-ledgers into evidence that convicts the Court by its own records. The beat is cost and triumph inseparable.

chapters.title: Salt in the Bread
chapters.summary: Resolution. Months later, magic is common property: taught in kitchens, not courts. Hazel, sword-less but not speechless, teaches charms beside Maren's rebuilt tithe-house-turned-school while Sebastian trains new ward-keepers. On the night the stars return, the three share bread under an open sky. The beat is quiet belonging—an inheritance refused, then remade, then given away.
